key_insight: Chemical concentration gradients in porous and crowded media can actively move colloids and droplets via diffusiophoresis and diffusioosmosis, strongly altering transport beyond classical dispersion and filtration.
engineering_relevance: This matters for designing filters, soil remediation, tissue transport, hydrogel delivery, and microfluidic systems where chemical fronts can either enhance removal or dramatically change breakthrough.
method: Review of sources that generate and sustain solute gradients in complex media
Minimal physicochemical framework for diffusiophoresis and diffusioosmosis
Comparison with classical colloid-transport mechanisms and experimental platforms
evidence_signal: The abstract synthesizes recent experimental findings showing that diffuse solute fronts can prolong phoretic forcing in dead-end pores and that cross-streamline migration can change breakthrough and dispersion by orders of magnitude.
watch_item: Effects depend strongly on gradient structure, pore geometry, and dimensionality, so results from 2D micromodels may not directly transfer to real 3D porous media.
paper_title: Diffusiophoretic transport of colloids and emulsions in complex environments
